runs_note: The exact run set this key was authored from; scoring must replay these and only these.
audit_note: The adversarial pass challenged this family's keys harder than any other's. A key flagged audit_challenged carries load-bearing defects its own auditor found; a score computed against it measures the key as much as the system.
session_notes:
ONE FACT ORGANISES THIS WHOLE SESSION: the readout drive power changed by ~20-27 dB between run #3 and run #6, and the resonators moved with it. Runs #2 and #3 ran with port mw_outputs/con1/1/1 at full_scale_power_dbm = +13 (qA1 readout amp 0.0369 => ~-15.7 dBm at the port; qA2 amp 0.0791 => ~-9.0 dBm) - deep in the punch-out regime. Run #4 (05b_resonator_spectroscopy_vs_power_iq, 03:56, out of family) dropped FSP to -11 and run #9 (05b, 04:11) re-optimised the per-qubit amplitudes; every run from #6 onward sat at ~-33 to -40 dBm. Verified against the raw cubes: at high power qA1's ONLY notch is at 7.122675 GHz (13.9 sigma) and there is nothing at 7.1259 (+1.1 sigma); at operating power the ONLY notch is at 7.125882 GHz (5.6-8.7 sigma) and there is nothing at 7.1227 (-0.6 sigma). Same for qA2: 7.392084 (37 sigma) at high power vs 7.394527 (14-22 sigma) after. Both high-power lines are deeper AND narrower (qA2 FWHM 0.245 MHz vs 0.744 MHz after) - the punch-out signature. So run #3's fits were CORRECT MEASUREMENTS OF THE WRONG OPERATING POINT, and committing them to resonator/f_01 + RF_frequency before the readout power had ever been calibrated is the session's only real error. It cost the state its previously-correct values (qA1 7125775055.64, qA2 7393783578.29 - within 0.15 and 0.74 MHz of the eventual truth), mis-seeded run #6's sweep centre and fit start, produced #6's failed 7.110215 GHz / 8.65 MHz "fit", and cost run #7.

THE FAMILY'S OWN HAZARD IS ALSO HERE, TWICE. qA1 and qA6 are strongly Fano-asymmetric at the operating power: a narrow notch with a LARGER peak 1.8-2.5 MHz above it on a steeply structured background. On qA6 the Lorentzian cannot model the peak, so r2 falls to 0.831 and the OLD-generation node - which has only frequency/fwhm/r2/success and no success_shape, dip_snr or candidates field - reports the whole target "failed" and writes nothing. But the fitted f0 = 7.758176699 GHz sits 11 kHz from the raw minimum, and the detrended-phase panel shows a full dispersive S with its zero-crossing exactly there. That is a shape verdict masquerading as a frequency failure; the newer generation would have said "frequency OK, shape poor". The four-panel cross-check (amplitude notch + phase wrap + IQ circle) is what settles it, and it settles all six qubits of run #10 in one look: every one of the six has a clean dispersive phase residual centred on its marked f0, including the two the amplitude panel alone would leave ambiguous.

THE WIDE SCAN COULD NEVER HAVE WORKED. Run #2's band is 7.19995-7.49980 GHz; qA1's resonator is at 7.1258 GHz, 74 MHz below the low edge, while the run's own init_rf_hz records 7.125775 - the node swept a band that excludes the estimate it was given. For qA2 the band did cover the line and a 6.9 sigma notch is present at 7.392100 in that very data, but the candidate ranker returned 7.3228 (3.7-5.9 dB), 7.4647, 7.3092 GHz - none within 26 MHz of the stored value - and the fit returned NaN. Neither failure was a chip problem.

OPERATOR SCORECARD: the operator reached the right end state for qA1-qA5 and did so without ever adopting a wrong-feature fit, which is the main way this family goes wrong. They spent 7 in-family runs where 4 were needed on qA1, 6 where 3 were needed on qA2, and they lost qA6 to a verdict they should have overridden. Runs #8 (both fits succeeded, node wrote NOTHING) and #58 (10 hours later, agreed within 47 kHz on qA1 and 20 kHz on qA2) changed no decision, though #58 is defensible as a start-of-afternoon drift check before the CR work.

ONE LOST WRITE, NOT A POISONED ONE: run #10's patches for qA3/qA4/qA5 did land, but by run #58 the state holds their pre-#10 values again (7479776069.67 / 7248088279.27 / 7662321872.96) and the readout amplitudes have reverted to their pre-#4 values too - the state was rolled back or reloaded from another copy between 04:17 and 14:20. Numerically harmless (81-147 kHz, all << 1 FWHM) but those three calibrations did not survive the day. Out of scope but worth knowing: the later 15a_readout_frequency_optimization runs (#43, #67) deliberately offset f_01 by -400/-200 kHz for discrimination; those are not resonance measurements and must not be read as disagreeing with the 03 values.

FIGURE BUDGET USED: 3 of 6 - run #10 amplitude (settles qA6's Fano shape and qA1's asymmetry, and covers 4 targets at once), run #10 detrended_phase (settles that all six notches, qA6 included, are real resonances), run #3 amplitude (settles that the high-power lines are single clean notches, i.e. power-shifted rather than wrong-feature picks). Everything else was decided numerically from ds_raw.h5/ds_fit.h5: baseline-subtracted dip SNR, dip position, linear-detrended phase deviation at the fitted f0, and per-run readout power computed as FSP + 20*log10(amp) from each run's own quam_state snapshot.
adversarial_audit:
Audited against the archive at `D:\work\dataset\KRISS_CR\2026-06-17`. The key's physics core is sound; its bookkeeping and one evidence claim are not.

**Defects**

1. **qA3/qA4/qA5 · #10 — "independent corroboration" is the operator's own last run.** The priors 7479976069.67 / 7248288279.27 / 7662421872.96 were written by **run #9** (05b, 6 min earlier) as exact **+200/+200/+100 kHz** steps off the pre-existing values — fractional digits preserved to the last decimal, i.e. a 100 kHz grid offset, not a measurement. *Correction:* cite the genuine pre-session prior (…776069.67 / …088279.27 / …321872.96), which agrees **better — 89/53/18 kHz, not the quoted 111/147/82** — and drop "independent".

2. **session_notes/caveats vs value_evidence — contradiction.** Both name …776069.67 / …088279.27 / …321872.96 as the "pre-#10 values"; #10's own patch `old` fields say pre-#10 was 200/200/100 kHz higher. Those are **pre-#9** values. *Correction:* relabel.

3. **Rollback scope understated.** "Those three calibrations did not survive the day" is false: at **#57** all **six** qubits revert to pre-session — qA1 7.125775, qA2 7.393784 — wiping #6/#7/#10 and all four of #9's writes. That is precisely why #58's patches carry those as `old`. *Correction:* six lost, not three; the "right end state for qA1–qA5" claim needs qualifying.

4. **Rollback window wrong.** Not "04:17–14:20": **#43 (08:58) still holds post-#10 values**, #57 (14:06) is already reverted. *Correction:* 08:58–14:06.

5. **qA1 · ideal_length=4 / termination #7 — self-contradictory.** Step 3 says "re-fit… no new data needed" and wasted_runs charges #7 to the poisoned write; yet #7 is step 4 and the termination. Without the #3 write, #6 is centred on 7.1258 and fits — as it did for **qA2 in that same run**. *Correction:* ideal_length **3**, terminate at **#6**, symmetric with qA2.

6. **qA6 · #10 — overclaim on the key's one override.** Detrending on resonance-free edges, qA6's zero-crossing is **311 kHz = 0.28 FWHM** from f0 — second-worst of six (qA5 19 kHz, qA2 66, qA3 89, qA4 153, qA1 396). Not "exactly there", not "panel-for-panel" with the five. Verdict survives; the evidence must be stated at true tightness. (Excursion −0.26/+0.70 rad ✓.)

7. **qA6 caveat — wrong mechanism.** #9 set qA6 amp to **0.0214**, not "~0.05–0.09"; the 0.0824 at #10 came from an unrecorded change after #9, and #4's 1.518 was already gone by **#5**. No-clipping conclusion holds.

8. **Minor.** "Every run from #6 onward −33 to −40 dBm" — qA3/4/5 were −16.9/−20.9/−19.4 at #6–#8, −40.9/−44.9/−43.4 at #58. "20–27 dB" → 19–27. qA2 prominences are 2.3–5.9 dB (3.7 is qA1's); "within 26 MHz" is unsourced — true minimum is 71 MHz.

**Verified sound:** every fit value (f0/FWHM/r²/success) to the digit; the punch-out thesis (dip positions, FSP+20log|amp|, the 7.1227↔7.1259 exclusion); #2's band/`init_rf_hz`/candidates; #8's absent `patches` key; the −400/−200 kHz #43/#67 offsets.

ideal_path.expected_case: Old generation. The wide sweep covers 7.19995-7.49980 GHz; qA1's stored resonator estimate is 7.125775 GHz - 74 MHz BELOW the low edge, and the run's own init_rf_hz field records that estimate. The band cannot contain the target, so the NaN fit and r2=0 say nothing about the chip. The four returned candidates (7.3180 / 7.2358 / 7.3410 / 7.3927 GHz, 2.2-3.7 dB prominence) are other structure in the feedline, none of them qA1. Compounding it, the port is at full_scale_power_dbm=+13 with readout amp 0.0369, i.e. ~-15.7 dBm at the resonator - far above the dispersive regime.
ideal_path.correct_next_action: Discard this run for qA1 - it is a configuration error, not a measurement. Re-point the sweep so it brackets the stored 7.1258 GHz (band 7.05-7.25 GHz), or go straight to 03 single with frequency_span_in_mhz=30, frequency_step_in_mhz=0.1 centred on 7.1258 GHz. Before either, cut the readout drive: run the 05b readout-power calibration first, or at minimum drop the port FSP from +13 dBm, because a resonance measured at this drive will not be the one the chip is read out at.
ideal_path.operator_did: Went straight to 03 single-span at the stored centre (run #3) without touching the readout power.

ideal_path.expected_case: Old generation, span 30 MHz / step 0.1 MHz, window 7.11078-7.14068 GHz. A single clean notch at 7.122675 GHz, 13.9 sigma against the cubic baseline, FWHM 0.741 MHz, r2 0.979, with a coincident dispersive phase residual - a REAL resonance, not a Fano side-lobe (the amplitude panel shows one dip and no competing peak). But it is a HIGH-POWER resonance: this run still has FSP +13 dBm (~-15.7 dBm at the resonator), the R baseline is 45-60 mV, and the value is 3.093 MHz - 4.2 of its own linewidths - BELOW the stored 7.125775 GHz. The window also contains 7.1259 GHz, where this data shows nothing (+1.1 sigma), so at this drive there is exactly one line and it has moved.
ideal_path.correct_next_action: Record 7.122682 GHz as a high-power observation but do NOT write resonator/f_01 or RF_frequency. Run the readout-power calibration (05b) to set the operating drive, then repeat 03 single at that drive with span 30 MHz / step 0.1 MHz centred on the STORED 7.1258 GHz, and commit only from that repeat. A resonator frequency taken before the readout power exists is provisional by construction.
ideal_path.operator_did: Adopted: wrote 7122681560.80 Hz to /quam/qubits/qA1/resonator/f_01 and /RF_frequency, replacing the correct 7125775055.64.

ideal_path.expected_case: First run at the calibrated drive (FSP -11, amp 0.0646 => -34.8 dBm, ~19 dB below run #3). Window 7.10768-7.13758 GHz, centred on the poisoned 7.12268. The failure is the fit's, not the data's; the value is already in hand.
ideal_path.correct_next_action: Reject the reported fit and recover the value from this acquisition: re-fit in a narrow window on the visible notch - re_fit_resonators=['qA1'], re_fit_centers_ghz=[7.1259], re_fit_span_mhz=4 - no new data needed. Repair the state at the same time: f_01/RF_frequency = 7.1259 GHz so the next sweep is centred on the real line. Do not widen the span and do not add shots; SNR is not the problem.

termination.reason: First clean fit at the calibrated readout power, with all three panels agreeing (amplitude notch at 7.125882, dispersive phase residual centred on the fitted f0, closed IQ arc). The value is stable across every subsequent run, so nothing after #7 changes the answer.
termination.value_evidence: Notch at 7.125882 GHz in #6 (5.6 sigma), #7 (6.5 sigma) and #8 (5.9 sigma); 7.125922 in #10 (8.7 sigma) and 7.125975 in #58 (5.7 sigma), each with a detrended-phase zero-crossing on the fitted centre. wasted_runs.why_wasted: The swept band (7.19995-7.49980 GHz) does not contain qA1's resonator at all - 74 MHz outside - while the run's own init_rf_hz recorded 7.125775 GHz. No possible outcome of this acquisition could have informed qA1. It stays in the ideal path only because the replay must render the verdict 'mis-configured band, reject' on it.

Not wasted in the operator's path (it produced the committed value), but it exists only because run #6's failed fit was re-acquired rather than re-fitted. A re-fit of #6's own data in a 4 MHz window on the visible notch would have produced the same number without a second acquisition. Charged to the run-#3 poisoned write, which put #6's fit start where there is no feature.

Pure repeat of #7 six minutes later, same drive, agrees to 8.7 kHz - and the node wrote NOTHING (node.json carries no patches key at all), so it did not even refresh the state. No decision depended on it.

Redundant for qA1 (third confirmation of 7.1259 in 15 minutes, Delta -3.6 kHz). The run itself is necessary and correct - it is the only measurement qA3-qA6 ever get - so this is redundancy of a target within a needed run, not a wasted acquisition.

Ten-hour drift re-check before the CR work; agreed within 47 kHz and changed no decision or downstream action. Defensible as a start-of-afternoon sanity check, but not part of the shortest correct path.

poisoned_writes.why: Wrote 7122681560.80 Hz - a genuine resonance, but the one the resonator shows at the uncalibrated +13 dBm FSP drive (~-15.7 dBm at the port). Fifteen minutes later run #4 dropped the drive ~19 dB and the line moved to 7.125922 GHz, leaving the state 3.241 MHz (3.0 operating-power linewidths) off. It also overwrote the previously correct 7125775055.64 Hz, and it mis-seeded run #6: that run's sweep centre and fit start landed at 7.12268 where the low-power data has no feature, producing the failed 7.110215 GHz / 8.65 MHz fit and forcing the extra run #7. Corrected 26 minutes later by #7.

qubits.caveats: The power-shift diagnosis is not an inference from the fits - it is read directly from the raw cubes: at high power qA1 shows one notch at 7.122675 and +1.1 sigma at 7.1259; at operating power it shows one notch at 7.125882 and -0.6 sigma at 7.1227. Per-run readout power was computed as FSP + 20*log10(readout amplitude) from each run's own quam_state snapshot (+13 dBm/0.0369 => -15.7 dBm at #2/#3; -11 dBm/0.0646 => -34.8 dBm at #6-#10; -11 dBm/0.0369 => -39.7 dBm at #58). Judgement call flagged: at run #3's cursor a reader who adopts is not being reckless - the notch is real and confirmed by phase - so 'reconfirm' is graded on the rule 'never commit a resonator frequency taken before the readout power is calibrated', which the run sequence (05b immediately next) makes visible. A grader may reasonably score adopt-at-#3 as a soft error rather than a hard one; what is NOT defensible is failing to notice at #6 that the state had moved. Note also that the amplitude panel alone is ambiguous for qA1 at operating power - the Fano peak ~2.5 MHz above the notch is comparable in excursion to the dip - so the phase panel is doing real work here, not decoration.

One cosmetic note for anyone re-deriving from the raw cube: qA5's largest linear-detrended phase excursion sits ~300 kHz off the notch because the S-curve's negative lobe is broader than its positive one; the zero-crossing, which is the correct marker, is on f0.

ideal_path.expected_case: THE FANO CASE, and the one the operator got wrong. Old generation, calibrated drive (qA6 amp 0.0824 => -32.7 dBm), span 20 MHz / step 0.1 MHz. The amplitude panel is strongly asymmetric: a sharp notch at 7.758166 GHz dropping to ~6 mV from an ~11 mV baseline, with a LARGER excursion - a peak reaching ~16 mV - 1.8 MHz above it, and a second broad hump ~4 MHz below; the tallest feature in the panel is NOT the resonance. The Lorentzian cannot represent that structure, so r2 falls to 0.831, the node returns success=false and writes nothing. But the fitted f0 = 7.758176699 GHz sits 11 kHz from the raw minimum (5.9 sigma), and the detrended-phase panel shows a full dispersive S with its zero-crossing exactly there, matching the five accepted qubits panel-for-panel. This is a SHAPE failure reported as a target failure: the newer node generation would have split it into success=true / success_shape=false with a dip_snr and a candidate list; the old one cannot say it.
ideal_path.correct_next_action: Override the node's verdict on the FREQUENCY only: write f_01 = RF_frequency = 7.758177 GHz, and record that the shape verdict failed so no linewidth/Q is claimed from this run. Do not re-run to 'fix' r2 by adding shots - SNR is not the limitation, the asymmetric background is. If a usable lineshape is genuinely wanted later, re-run qA6 alone with frequency_span_in_mhz=40 so the peak and both background humps sit inside the fit window; that is a shape question, not a frequency one, and it is not needed to proceed.
ideal_path.operator_did: Accepted the node's failure: no patch, leaving qA6 on the stale 7758265665.75 Hz, and never re-measured it in the session.

termination.reason: The only qA6 measurement of the session, and it is sufficient: the frequency is settled by the cross-panel check even though the amplitude fit's shape verdict correctly failed. Re-running would answer a question nobody needed answered.
termination.value_evidence: Raw-cube minimum at 7.758166 GHz, 5.9 sigma against the cubic baseline, with the reported f0 7.758177 GHz landing 11 kHz away; the detrended-phase panel shows a complete dispersive S (excursion -0.27 to +0.72 rad) with its zero-crossing on that f0 - the same signature as the five accepted qubits in the same run. The stale state value 7758265665.75 Hz agrees to 89 kHz = 0.08 FWHM, so nothing contradicts it. Confidence is capped at med because there is exactly one acquisition, the amplitude fit is genuinely poor (r2 0.831) so the FWHM 1.104 MHz should not be trusted, and the neighbouring peak is only 1.4x weaker than the notch in SNR terms - this is the shape most likely to fool a re-fit.

qubits.caveats: This is the session's one target where the ideal path lands somewhere the operator never went: adopting a value the node itself declared failed. The justification is the four-figure cross-check that this family alone provides - amplitude notch, phase wrap, IQ closure - and it is decision-hinging here, which is why a figure was spent on it. Two honest limits. First, the practical stake is small: the stale value the operator left in place is 89 kHz (0.08 FWHM) from the measurement, so the chip was not badly mis-configured by the omission; the error is procedural (no measurement ever backed the number) more than numerical. Second, if a grader insists that a target whose only fit failed must be scored unresolved, that is a defensible stricter reading - but it would have to discard the phase evidence, and the same evidence is what validates the five qubits scored successful in that identical run. The linewidth from this run is NOT usable: r2 0.831 means the reported FWHM 1.104 MHz is contaminated by the adjacent peak. Also note the readout amplitude here is 0.0824 at FSP -11 dBm, i.e. no DAC clipping and no over-drive - an earlier hypothesis that run #4's transient amplitude assignment (1.518 for qA6) caused the poor shape is REFUTED: run #9 re-set every amplitude to the ~0.05-0.09 range before run #10 executed.
